dedupe_keys.name: 5gmdata ray traced 60 ghz mmwave mimo channel data with vehicle mobility for 5g machine learning lasse ufpa

description: 5GMdata provides datasets and code for machine learning on 5G millimetre-wave MIMO systems with moving users, built by combining vehicle mobility simulation with ray-tracing of radio propagation. It comes from the LASSE group at the Federal University of Pará (UFPA) in Brazil and was introduced by Klautau, Batista, Gonzalez-Prelcic, Wang and Heath at the 2018 Information Theory and Applications workshop, where it was applied to beam selection with deep learning. Coverage: the urban_canyon_v2i 5gmv1 dataset simulates 60 GHz vehicle-to-infrastructure links in an urban canyon: 116 episodes of 50 scenes each (5,800 ray-tracing runs at 100 ms intervals), one roadside transmitter and up to 10 receivers on cars, giving 41,023 valid channels with the 25 strongest rays each; the wiki points to the later Raymobtime datasets from the same group. Format and access: SQLite databases, HDF5 and NumPy NPZ files split by episode, and raw Remcom Wireless InSite outputs, downloadable from the group's Nextcloud, with Python and MATLAB code on GitHub; free. Licence: GPL-3.0 for the code (LICENSE file); no separate data licence stated. Caveats: the data are simulated for one synthetic scenario with omnidirectional antennas, the repository has not changed since May 2022, and the Raymobtime site answered a server error so the newer datasets were not read. Simulation uses: training beam-selection and channel models for connected-vehicle communication in digital twin and cascading failure studies of transport and telecom interaction. Related records: Veins (model-veins-vehicular-network-simulation) simulates vehicular communication at network level.
